outcome: Clinical features of hemiplegic cerebral palsy
cohort: The study included 144 children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy (95 with perinatal arterial ischemic stroke and 49 with periventricular venous infarction) enrolled at 9 rehabilitation centers across Ontario.
finding: Neonatal systemic thrombosis, emergency cesarean section, and neonatal seizures were more frequently associated with hemiplegic cerebral palsy in children with perinatal arterial ischemic stroke than with periventricular venous infarction.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean section was identified as a clinical feature associated with hemiplegic cerebral palsy in children with perinatal arterial ischemic stroke more often than periventricular venous infarction.
